posts.title: The first roast of autumn
posts.excerpt: The roaster came back on last Wednesday after the summer rest. A note on the first beans of the season.
posts.content:
The roaster came back on last Wednesday after the summer rest. A note on the first beans of the season.

Waking the drum

After two months cold, the drum is run empty for an hour before a single bean goes in.

Ken listens to it more than he looks at it, and opens the window onto Kanzaki-dōri for the smell.

Tanzania first

The first batch is always the Tanzanian, because we know it best: if anything is off, we will taste it at once.

By midnight the print shop smelled of bread crust and dried cherries, and the season had begun.

A roast tells you when it is done, if you are quiet enough to hear it crack.

Ken Arima

posts.title: Why we temper by hand
posts.excerpt: A machine could do it. We still spread chocolate on a cold stone slab every night. Here is why.
posts.content:
A machine could do it. We still spread chocolate on a cold stone slab every night. Here is why.

On the stone

Tempering sets the cocoa butter into one small, stable crystal, which gives a bar its snap and its quiet shine.

On marble you can see it happen: the chocolate thickens, dulls a little, and begins to hold the line of the palette knife.

What the hand learns

Each origin behaves differently. The Belize is stubborn; the Peru goes soft in a warm room.

Working by hand keeps us close enough to notice, batch by batch.

The slab is the oldest tool in the kitchen, and still the most honest.

Nao Fujisaki

posts.title: Twelve squares in a box
posts.excerpt: How we choose the twelve bonbons in a box, and the order in which we suggest eating them.
posts.content:
How we choose the twelve bonbons in a box, and the order in which we suggest eating them.

Four rows, three columns

Each row holds one family: flowers and tea, then seeds, then nuts, then the darkest of the season.

We place them so that the lightest ganache sits nearest to the hand when the lid comes off.

Left to right

Start at the top left and move along the row, with a sip of water between rows.

There is no wrong order, but there is a gentle one.

A box should read like a short letter, one line at a time.

Nao Fujisaki

posts.title: Tea and cacao
posts.excerpt: Roasted tea and roasted cacao share more than a colour. Notes on our hōjicha ganache.
posts.content:
Roasted tea and roasted cacao share more than a colour. Notes on our hōjicha ganache.

Two roasts

Hōjicha is green tea roasted until it turns brown and sweet; its toasted note meets the cocoa of the Tanzanian bean halfway.

We steep the leaves in warm cream for exactly eight minutes, then strain and weigh what is left.

Less is more

Too long and the tea turns bitter, too short and it disappears behind the chocolate.

The square is finished with a dusting of ground leaf, so the scent arrives before the taste.

Tea should whisper in a bonbon, not speak over it.

Nao Fujisaki

posts.title: A night in the kitchen
posts.excerpt: We work when the street is asleep. A short account of one night, from closing time to first light.
posts.content:
We work when the street is asleep. A short account of one night, from closing time to first light.

Seven o'clock

The shop door closes, the counter is wiped down, and the kitchen at the back of the old print shop comes on.

Shells are cast first, while the room is still warm from the day.

Three in the morning

Ganache is piped, left to set, and sealed. The street outside is quiet enough to hear the moulds tap.

By dawn the trays are covered and labelled, ready for the cool room and the next afternoon.

Chocolate likes the dark and the cool. So, it turns out, do we.

Ken Arima

posts.title: Packing for a warm month
posts.excerpt: From mid-June we stop sending bonbons by post. What we do instead, and how tablets travel in summer.
posts.content:
From mid-June we stop sending bonbons by post. What we do instead, and how tablets travel in summer.

Why we pause

A filled bonbon does not survive a hot van: the ganache weeps and the shell blooms grey.

So from 15 June to 15 September bonbons stay in the shop, where you can still collect them on the day.

Tablets in cool packs

Tablets travel well if they are kept below twenty degrees, so we wrap them with a cool pack and send them early in the week.

When the evenings cool again, the boxes of twelve go back on the post.

Summer is for the shop counter; autumn is for the post.

Nao Fujisaki

products.name: Rose Clay Dome
products.short: A dome of Peruvian 66% filled with a soft rose-petal ganache.
products.description:
A dome of Peruvian 66% filled with a soft rose-petal ganache.

The shell is brushed with a clay-pink cocoa butter before casting. Inside, petals steeped in cream give a quiet floral note over the red-fruit of the Marañón bean.

Every piece is made by hand, so shape and finish vary slightly from the photograph. Bonbons are not sent by post from 15 June to 15 September.

products.name: Hōjicha Square
products.short: A square of Tanzanian 70% around a roasted-tea ganache.
products.description:
A square of Tanzanian 70% around a roasted-tea ganache.

Hōjicha leaves are steeped in warm cream for eight minutes, then folded into the chocolate. Toasted, a little sweet, finished with a dusting of ground leaf.

Every piece is made by hand, so shape and finish vary slightly from the photograph. Bonbons are not sent by post from 15 June to 15 September.

products.name: Black Sesame Swirl
products.short: A swirled shell of Vietnamese 72% with a roasted black-sesame praline.
products.description:
A swirled shell of Vietnamese 72% with a roasted black-sesame praline.

We roast the sesame ourselves and grind it slowly with a little sugar into a dark, nutty paste. The Tiền Giang bean adds spice and a long finish.

Every piece is made by hand, so shape and finish vary slightly from the photograph. Bonbons are not sent by post from 15 June to 15 September.

products.name: Hazelnut Praline Dome
products.short: A dark dome of Belizean 75% around a crisp hazelnut praline.
products.description:
A dark dome of Belizean 75% around a crisp hazelnut praline.

Hazelnuts are caramelised in copper, cooled on the slab and ground just short of smooth, so a little crunch remains under the deep, earthy chocolate.

Every piece is made by hand, so shape and finish vary slightly from the photograph. Bonbons are not sent by post from 15 June to 15 September.

products.name: Pistachio Square
products.short: A square of Peruvian 66% filled with a pale pistachio ganache.
products.description:
A square of Peruvian 66% filled with a pale pistachio ganache.

Roasted pistachio paste, a pinch of salt and the bright fruit of the Marañón bean. A green line across the top tells it apart in the box.

Every piece is made by hand, so shape and finish vary slightly from the photograph. Bonbons are not sent by post from 15 June to 15 September.

products.name: Walnut & Kuromitsu Oval
products.short: An oval of Tanzanian 70% with toasted walnut and a thread of black-sugar syrup.
products.description:
An oval of Tanzanian 70% with toasted walnut and a thread of black-sugar syrup.

Kuromitsu, a dark syrup of unrefined sugar, is folded into a walnut ganache. It brings a smoky sweetness that suits the first cold evenings.

Every piece is made by hand, so shape and finish vary slightly from the photograph. Bonbons are not sent by post from 15 June to 15 September.

products.name: Tanzania 70% Tablet
products.short: A single-origin tablet of Tanzanian cacao and cane sugar, nothing else.
products.description:
A single-origin tablet of Tanzanian cacao and cane sugar, nothing else.

Roasted in the old print shop, conched for three days and tempered by hand on stone. Notes of dried cherry, bread crust and a little honey.

Every piece is made by hand, so shape and finish vary slightly from the photograph. Bonbons are not sent by post from 15 June to 15 September.

products.name: Box of Twelve
products.short: Twelve bonbons in a ribbon box: two of each of the six of the season.
products.description:
Twelve bonbons in a ribbon box: two of each of the six of the season.

Set in four rows of three, from the lightest ganache to the darkest, with a small card that names each piece and its origin. Tied by hand with a ribbon.

Every piece is made by hand, so shape and finish vary slightly from the photograph. Bonbons are not sent by post from 15 June to 15 September.
